subproblem.title: Closure theorem in degree zero (CL(0))
subproblem.statement: Assume (REP), (MR) and (IMC). Here (REP), (MR), (IMC), (SL), (DT), (VO) denote the parent node's dependency theorems: (REP) and (IMC) are the first and second conjuncts of the frozen statement of dimred_mbl_current_foundations, (MR) is the mass identity of dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support (the first conjunct of its conclusion: M_W(T) = R.measure(W) for every IMRep R of T in an open U and every open W; its support identity is not needed), and (SL), (DT), (VO) are the frozen statements of dimred_mbl_slice_mass_bounds, dimred_mbl_deformation_theorem and dtc_vanish_off_support. They are not available in this child's environment, so the needed ones appear as hypotheses of the Lean statement ((REP), (IMC), (SL), (DT), (VO) verbatim, (MR) as the stated mass identity) and are discharged by the parent proof. In words: (REP) a current with locally finite mass in an open U has a mass representation (μ, ξ) (μ(W) = M_W for open W, μ(ℝ^P∖U) = 0, μ finite on compacts of U, |ξ| ≤ 1, X(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ, and μ(E) = 0 whenever Hⁿ(E) = 0 if also the boundary has locally finite mass); (MR) M_W(X) = R.measure(W) for an IMRep R of X and open W; (IMC) (a) locality of approximate tangent spaces for nested Borel sets, (b) the restriction of an IMRep to a Borel set is an IMRep of some current, (c) differences of IM currents are IM, (d) IMRep orientations satisfy |orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| a.e.; (SL) slicing by an L-Lipschitz f of a current represented together with its boundary, with Z_t := ∂(X⌞{f<t}) − (∂X)⌞{f<t} vanishing on forms supported off {f = t}, M_W(Z_t) ≤ L liminf_h h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t−h<f<t}) and the integrated bound; (DT) the deformation theorem with its mass and support bounds; (VO) a current vanishes on test forms whose support misses its support. For every P, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and T_j, T ∈ 𝒟_0(U): if every T_j is integer multiplicity, sup_j (M_W(T_j) + boundaryMassOn(T_j, W)) < ∞ for every open W with compact closure in U (the boundary term is 0 in degree 0), and T_j ⇀ T in U, then T is integer multiplicity.

B)) ∧ (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict R.carrier), ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |R.orient x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α)) → ∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (Ts : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U 0) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U 0), IsOpen U → (∀ j, IsIntegerMultiplicity (Ts j)) → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → ⨆ j, ((Ts j).massOn W + boundaryMassOn (Ts j) W) < ∞) → WeaklyConvergesOn Ts T → IsIntegerMultiplicity T
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Part III (CL(0)), with the final appeal to T4 made through the sibling theorem dmcbr_isIntegerMultiplicity_of_local (child im_local), whose hypotheses (REP), (MR), (IMC) (the relevant parts of the frozen statements of the parent node's dependency theorems dimred_mbl_current_foundations (first conjunct), dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support (mass identity), dimred_mbl_current_foundations (second conjunct); not available to this child, hence assumed) are hypotheses here. For a 0-covector α write ⟨α⟩ := α(∅) (the value on the empty tuple); α ↦ ⟨α⟩ identifies Covector(ℝ^P, 0) with ℝ, and |α| = |⟨α⟩|. A 0-form a ∈ 𝒟^0(U) is identified with the smooth function x ↦ ⟨a(x)⟩.

1. Degree-0 IMReps. H⁰ = μHE[0] = μH[0] (Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero) is the counting measure (μH[0]{x} = 1, Mathlib hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton; by additivity over singletons H⁰(S) = card S for finite S, and H⁰(S) = ∞ for infinite S, which contain countably infinitely many points; also 1 ≤ μH[0](S) for nonempty S, Mathlib one_le_hausdorffMeasure_zero_of_nonempty). Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep in U of S ∈ 𝒟_0(U). (i) For compact K ⊆ U, Σ_{x∈M∩K} θ(x) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dH⁰ < ∞ and θ ≥ 1 on M, so M ∩ K is finite. (ii) The only H⁰-null subset of M is ∅, so the orientation property of R holds at every x ∈ M: ξ(x) is a unit orientation of a 0-dimensional subspace; by the definition IsUnitOrientationOf with n = 0 (the orthonormal family is the empty family) ξ(x)(α) = ε(x)⟨α⟩ with ε(x) ∈ {1, −1}. (iii) Hence, with m(x) := ε(x)θ(x) ∈ ℤ ∖ {0}, S(a) = Σ_{x∈M} m(x)⟨a(x)⟩ for a ∈ 𝒟^0(U) (a finite sum: only x ∈ M ∩ tsupport a contribute). (iv) By (MR), for open G, M_G(S) = R.measure(G) = Σ_{x∈M∩G} θ(x) = Σ_{x∈M∩G} |m(x)|.
2. Locally finite mass of T. For open W ⊂⊂ U, M_W(T) ≤ liminf_j M_W(T_j) (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf) ≤ sup_j (M_W(T_j) + boundaryMassOn(T_j, W)) < ∞ (boundaryMassOn is 0 in degree 0, and M_W(T_j) is bounded by the hypothesis).
3. Fix x₀ ∈ U and r > 0 with B̄_{2r}(x₀) ⊆ U. The open set B_{2r}(x₀) has compact closure in U, so c := sup_j M_{B_{2r}(x₀)}(T_j) < ∞. Let R_j = (M_j, θ_j, ξ_j) be IMReps of T_j and m_j as in step 1. By 1(iv), Σ_{x∈M_j∩B_{2r}(x₀)} |m_j(x)| ≤ c. Listing each x ∈ M_j ∩ B_{2r}(x₀) exactly |m_j(x)| times with sign ε_j(x): T_j(a) = Σ_{i=1}^{N_j} ε_{j,i}⟨a(x_{j,i})⟩ for all a ∈ 𝒟^0(U) with tsupport a ⊆ B_{2r}(x₀), where N_j ≤ c, ε_{j,i} ∈ {±1} and x_{j,i} ∈ B_{2r}(x₀).
4. N_j takes values in the finite set {0, …, ⌊c⌋} and (ε_{j,1}, …, ε_{j,N}) in the finite set {±1}^N, and B̄_{2r}(x₀)^N is compact; hence there is a subsequence (not relabeled; it still converges weakly to T) with N_j = N, ε_{j,i} = ε_i and x_{j,i} → y_i ∈ B̄_{2r}(x₀) for i = 1, …, N.
5. For a ∈ 𝒟^0(U) with tsupport a ⊆ B_r(x₀): T(a) = lim_j T_j(a) = lim_j Σ_{i=1}^N ε_i⟨a(x_{j,i})⟩ = Σ_{i=1}^N ε_i⟨a(y_i)⟩ (a continuous). Let Y := {y_1, …, y_N}, m(y) := Σ_{i: y_i = y} ε_i ∈ ℤ for y ∈ Y and F := {y ∈ Y ∩ B_r(x₀) : m(y) ≠ 0}, a finite subset of B_r(x₀). Since a vanishes on Y ∖ B_r(x₀) (outside tsupport a), T(a) = Σ_{y∈F} m(y)⟨a(y)⟩.
6. The domain restriction T|_{B_r(x₀)} ∈ 𝒟_0(B_r(x₀)) is integer multiplicity. Define an IMRep in B_r(x₀): carrier F; mult(y) := |m(y)| for y ∈ F, 0 otherwise; orient(y)(α) := sign(m(y))⟨α⟩ for y ∈ F, orient(y) := 0 otherwise. F is finite, hence Borel; it is countably 0-rectifiable (if F = ∅ by SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero; otherwise each point is the range of a constant, hence Lipschitz, map ℝ⁰ → ℝ^P; SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_range and countablyRectifiable_iUnion); mult and orient take finitely many values on finitely many points, so they are Borel/strongly measurable; mult > 0 on F; ∫_{F∩K} mult dH⁰ ≤ Σ_{y∈F}|m(y)| < ∞. Orientation at y ∈ F: the subspace {0} has finrank 0 and, with δ := dist(y, F ∖ {y}) > 0 (δ := ∞ if F = {y}), for f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with tsupport f ⊆ B_{R_f}(0) and 0 < ρ < δ/R_f, the blow-up blowUpMap y ρ (F) = ρ⁻¹(F − y) meets tsupport f at most in 0, so ∫_{blowUpMap y ρ '' F} f dH⁰ = f(0) = ∫_{{0}} f dH⁰; thus HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 F y {0}, and orient(y) = ±⟨·⟩ is a unit orientation of {0} (IsUnitOrientationOf with the empty orthonormal family). Representation: for a ∈ 𝒟^0(B_r(x₀)), the action is Σ_{y∈F} |m(y)| sign(m(y))⟨a(y)⟩ = Σ_{y∈F} m(y)⟨a(y)⟩ = T(a) = T|_{B_r(x₀)}(a) by step 5.
7. Steps 3–6 apply to every x₀ ∈ U (with some r > 0, B_r(x₀) ⊆ U). Together with step 2, part (1) of the sibling theorem dmcbr_isIntegerMultiplicity_of_local (applied with the hypotheses (REP), (MR), (IMC)) shows that T is integer multiplicity. ∎
proof_key_steps: Degree-0 IMReps are locally finite point sets with integer weights m(x) ≠ 0 (H⁰ is counting measure, orientations ±1), and by (MR) M_G = Σ|m| on open G.
T has locally finite mass by lower semicontinuity.
On B_{2r}(x₀) each T_j is a sum of at most c signed Dirac masses; pass to a subsequence with constant count and signs and convergent points.
On B_r(x₀), T equals a finite integer combination of Dirac masses, which is IM (explicit IMRep, approximate tangent space {0}).
